newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan urges caution on banking, commerce mix.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan urges caution on banking, commerce mix.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank Chairman Alan Greenspan on Thursday said that policymakers should move cautiously in mixing banking and commerce.
"Let me just say for the moment I think we ought to proceed with considerable caution on the question of division of the consolidation of banking and commerce," he said.

Speaking at a banking conference sponsored by the Chicago Fed, Greenspan said he took that position "mainly because we don't fully understand how the safety net and the subsidy will spill into various other different activities."
He said that as these various activities are expanded, the safety net that comes about because of deposit insurance should not go along with them.
Greenspan also told the conference he believed a role would remain for small banks despite the speed of technological change.
"I think there are certain aspects of finance which technology will never replace," he said.
Greenspan dismissed the idea of a global central bank, saying such an institution would only make problems such as that being faced by Japanese banks at this time even more difficult.
"I would say that the global central bank would only make the problem worse," he said.

In general, he said markets function in an effective manner because of private private regulation. "What we in government do is try to find ways that we can improve upon, not displace, regulation," he said.

He said that a global central bank would suggest a single global currency, adding "I hestitate to contemplate the implications of types of problems that would be involved on a regulatory, monetary and financial basis from trying to do something that complex."
